evidence.text:
Launch brief

Somebody has launched, but the page is not converting well.

What we know: signup conversion is weak, and many visitors do not immediately recognise that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies or understand how it differs from other AI tools.

The current page leans on broad "AI manager" and "automate your workflows" language. We suspect the positioning is too generic, but we do not yet have strong evidence for the words founders themselves use to describe the problem.

Prepare a stronger relaunch message for review today. Do not publish or send anything yet.

companyArtifacts.content:
Current launch page

Headline: "Somebody: an AI manager for your business."
Subhead: "Automate your workflows with AI."

Audience: General small businesses.
Current result: Signups are weaker than expected, and visitors often leave without clearly understanding who Somebody is for or why it is different from other AI tools.
Status: The current message is live. Any replacement should remain a draft until it is reviewed.

Diagnosis of current launch messaging (for review)

Evidence source: company record launch/context (Launch brief), observed as ev_1790158005570_m8loqj and re-read as ev_1790158038247_j9y03v.

Observed symptom: Signup conversion is weak. This is a reported performance outcome, not by itself a diagnosis of its cause.

Affected audience: Visitors who are founders running very small companies, including one-person companies and lean teams. The brief reports that many visitors do not immediately recognize that Somebody is built for this audience.

Affected messaging elements: The headline's broad "AI manager" framing and the subhead's broad "automate your workflows" framing. The brief reports that visitors often do not understand how Somebody differs from other AI tools.

Material failure mode indicated by the evidence: Audience and differentiation clarity are insufficient in the current message. The message does not make the intended founder audience or distinct value clear enough to many visitors.

Unconfirmed hypothesis: The positioning may be too generic because of the broad language above, but the launch brief does not establish that as a proven causal explanation. There is also no strong evidence yet for the words founders themselves use to describe the problem. Do not treat either point as validated.

Evidence base (assembled for relaunch review; not publication copy)

Source: company record launch/context (Launch brief)
- Reported performance: signup conversion is weak.
- Reported audience response: many visitors do not immediately recognize that Somebody is built for founders running very small companies or understand how it differs from other AI tools.
- Current messaging context: the page leans on broad “AI manager” and “automate your workflows” language.
- Evidence gap: the launch brief says there is not yet strong evidence for the words founders themselves use to describe the problem.

Revised launch messaging package (for review only; do not publish or send)

Headline: “An AI manager for founders running a one-person company.”
Subhead: “Somebody keeps important work moving—organising the work, bringing in help when needed, and staying with the job until there is a usable result.”

Audience: Founders running one-person companies and lean teams.

Rationale: Make the intended audience explicit in the headline and replace broad workflow-automation language with a practical description of what Somebody does: organising work, bringing in help when needed, and staying with the job until there is a usable result. This directly addresses the documented audience-recognition and differentiation-clarity failure modes without implying that Somebody replaces the founder or guarantees a business result.

Positioning note: Keep the message practical and outcome-focused. Do not imply that Somebody replaces the founder or guarantees a business result.

Measurable comparison criteria: Evaluate this draft against the current live message using the same audience, traffic conditions, measurement definitions, and test period. Compare (1) signup conversion rate, to determine whether the revised message produces more signups per visit; (2) immediate audience recognition, measured by the share of visitors who identify Somebody as intended for founders running one-person companies or lean teams; and (3) differentiation understanding, measured by the share of visitors who can explain how Somebody differs from other AI tools. The revised message is better only if the review records the observed baseline and comparison results and shows improvement on the selected criteria; no baseline, sample size, test period, or improvement threshold is supplied yet, so none is asserted here.

Review note: This draft addresses the documented clarity gap, but its performance and fit have not yet been tested. Founder-language research and quantitative baseline/testing data are still needed before treating the diagnosis or relaunch as validated or publishing it.

Next evidence needed before treating the diagnosis or relaunch as validated: founder-language research and quantitative baseline/testing data.

objective.request: Our launch messaging isn’t working. Figure out what’s wrong and get a better relaunch ready. You can spend within the approved limit if it’s justified.
objective.title: Our launch messaging isn’t working. Figure out what’s wro…

outcome.intent: Determine why the current launch messaging is underperforming and produce a relaunch messaging package that is ready for execution and evaluation.

levels.label: Diagnosis complete
levels.statement: The current launch messaging has a documented, evidence-based diagnosis identifying the material failure modes, affected audience, and supporting evidence.

levels.label: Relaunch specification ready
levels.statement: A revised launch messaging direction is defined, tied to the diagnosis, and accompanied by explicit criteria for judging whether it is better than the current messaging.

levels.label: Relaunch ready
levels.statement: The launch relaunch package is complete for the launch/page-message scope, including revised messaging, intended audience and positioning, rationale linked to the diagnosis, and measurable evaluation criteria.

requirements.mustBeTrue: The current launch messaging and the available evidence about its performance, audience response, and relevant launch context are assembled into a verifiable evidence base.
requirements.title: Launch messaging evidence established

requirements.mustBeTrue: The current launch messaging has a documented diagnosis that distinguishes the material failure modes from symptoms, identifies the affected audience and messaging elements, and links each conclusion to the evidence base.
requirements.title: Messaging failure diagnosed

requirements.mustBeTrue: A revised launch messaging package exists for the intended audience, addresses the diagnosed failure modes, states its rationale, and defines measurable criteria for determining whether it is better than the current messaging.
requirements.title: Relaunch messaging package ready
